title: Origami
description: Origami, in origami look cinematography, is paper as lawful sculpture: creases, planar color, a person or city becoming a fold. The world folds, and torn pulp without crease law is paper, not this.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Myths, titles, a delicate threat: visible creases, hard studio or sun, edges sharp. A living figure can be paper or stand among folds.
A person holding a paper crane as a prop is a craft-table extra, not the look. It is the wrong tool for a muddy war still, and the wrong tool if the stock is torn fiber with no facets.
Crease as line.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Origami in film?
Paper as sculpture: lawful creases, planar color, a person or city becoming a fold. The world folds. A prop crane is not the look.
Origami vs Paper
Paper is pulp, tear, fiber, cut-out. Origami is crease and facet. Tear versus fold.
When should I use Origami?
Myths, titles, delicate threat. Skip muddy war stills and craft-table extras.
How do I prompt Origami for AI image or video?
Hard light, then: Origami world of [Subject], lawful creases, planar color, a person or city becoming a fold. Demand creases. Forbid a handheld crane as the only paper.
